faqs.question: Can the Epson ink cartridges be refilled or can I use third-party ink cartridges without voiding the warranty?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend refilling or using other brands of ink cartridges.  Epson uses a permanent Micro Piezo print head that has allowed Epson to lead the industry in delivering consistent photo image quality by using variable-sized droplets.  Micro Piezo print head can also use a wider variety of inks, which has allowed Epson to introduce such ink breakthroughs as DURABrite® and Epson UltraChrome® inks that offer greatly improved humidity resistance, smudge resistance, and fade resistance.
Using refilled ink cartridges will not void the product's original warranty; however, if these products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: When I try to print to my product in Windows 7, printing is slow or my product stops printing. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Select a lower quality setting in the printer software.
Make sure your system meets the minimum system requirements for your printer.
Close the
Devices and Printers
window before you print.
Clear space on your hard drive or run a defragmentation utility.
Close programs that you're not using.
Increase your system's memory.

faqs.question: I brought my product with me to a different country and can't find ink for it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Some Epson printers and ink cartridges are specific to a regional market and not sold worldwide, although the same printers are sold in the U.S. and Canada. If you have a printer sold in the U.S. or Canada, you may not be able to easily get ink cartridges for it in foreign markets.
Unfortunately, because of customs and tax regulations, the Epson E-Stores in the U.S. and Canada are unable to ship to addresses outside the U.S. and Canada.

faqs.question: My product makes noise after I turn it on or after it has been sitting for a while. What should I do?
faqs.answer: This is normal. It is performing routine maintenance.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

faqs.question: Does my product have a factory reset button?
faqs.answer:
Yes, you can reset the print settings to their original, default values. Press and hold down the
Cancel
button for 3 seconds. When the message to reset the printer to default settings appears, press
OK
to reset the print settings.
Note: This reset does not affect LCD contrast, Print Confirmation, or PictureMate Print Wizard settings.

faqs.question: Why does the wrong photo print?
faqs.answer:
The photo numbering on the proof sheet may not match the numbering in your camera.
If you're printing without a computer, first print a proof sheet to identify your photos by number. If you deleted photos from your card or took new photos, you may need to
print a new proof sheet
.
If your camera supports DPOF, you can pre-select photos so PictureMate knows exactly what to print. See
Camera-selected DPOF Photos
in the User's Guide for more information.
If your camera is PictBridge-enabled or USB DP-enabled, you can connect it to PictureMate and control printing from the camera. See
Printing From a PictBridge-enabled Digital Camera
in the User's Guide for details.

faqs.question: Why doesn't my product see any photos on the memory card?
faqs.answer: Make sure photos are in JPEG or uncompressed Tiff format and taken with a DCF-compliant digital camera. Also, make sure only one memory card is inserted at a time.

faqs.question: I deleted some photos from my memory card and now it isn't working in my camera. What should I do?
faqs.answer: If you use your computer to delete pictures from a memory card, the card may not work correctly with your camera. If this happens, back up the memory card pictures to your computer, then use the camera to format the card. Remember to always delete your camera's pictures using your camera, not your computer.

faqs.question: Can my product read multiple memory cards at the same time?
faqs.answer: No. Insert just one card at a time.

faqs.question: Can my product read the images on my memory card that were saved in Adobe Photoshop?
faqs.answer: PictureMate cannot read files that have been opened and saved in Adobe Photoshop using the progressive save option. Files must be saved using the standard option.

faqs.question: Multiple pages are feeding into my product at the same time. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Remove the paper from the feeder, separate the sheets, and carefully reload the paper.

faqs.question: Paper jammed in my product. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Remove the paper, then press the
OK
button to clear the message. To prevent paper from jamming, see
Problems With Paper Feeding
in the User's Guide.

faqs.question: The paper will not feed correctly. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
See
Problems With Paper Feeding
in the User's Guide.

faqs.question: What types of paper can I use with my product?
faqs.answer:
See
Supported Paper Types
in the User's Guide.

faqs.question: Can I print on plain paper with my product?
faqs.answer: No. Don't load plain paper, as this may cause damage to PictureMate.

faqs.question: How long will my photos last?
faqs.answer: Using the PictureMate cartridge and PictureMate paper, prints are predicted to last up to 200 years when stored in archival sleeves in an album and up to 100 years when displayed indoors behind a glass frame.

faqs.answer:

You see banding

faqs.question: My product sounds as though it is printing, but nothing prints. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure the print head nozzles are not clogged. To clean the print head, see
Cleaning the Print Head
in the User's Guide.
PictureMate won't operate properly if it's tilted or at an angle. Place it on a flat, stable surface that extends beyond the base in all directions.

faqs.question: My product is printing blank pages from Windows or my Mac. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If blank pages are printing, try the following:
Make sure PictureMate is selected, or is the active printer in the Print Center or Macintosh Chooser.
The print head may need cleaning; see
Cleaning the Print Head
in the User's Guide for instructions.

faqs.question: Why is the size or position of my printed image wrong?
faqs.answer:
If the image size or position is incorrect, try the following:
Make sure the paper and layout options in your printer software settings (on the computer) or on the PictureMate Main Menu (printing without a computer) are set correctly.
Your photo size may not match the width/height proportions (aspect ratio) of the paper size or layout you're using. Photos may be cropped to fit the paper and layout.

faqs.question: My printout has incorrect margins. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If the margins are incorrect, try the following:
Make sure the paper is positioned correctly in the feeder, all the way to the right. Slide the left edge guide against the paper.
If you are printing without a computer, make sure the
Crop setting
is set to
Off
and check your
Layout setting
.

faqs.question: Is there a self test to determine if my print quality problem is caused by my product?
faqs.answer:
Yes, you can
run a printer check
to determine if a problem comes from PictureMate itself or some other source.

faqs.question: My images saved as CMYK do not look correct. What should I do?
faqs.answer: PictureMate automatically converts RGB images to CMYK. If the image is already CMYK, the color output will not be as expected. Try saving your images as RGB before printing.

faqs.question: Can I connect my digital camera to my product and print directly from the camera?
faqs.answer:
You can do this with a PictBridge-enabled or USB DP-enabled digital camera. See
Printing From a PictBridge-enabled Digital Camera
in the User's Guide for more information.

faqs.question: Can my product be networked?
faqs.answer:
PictureMate can be set up as a shared printer. See
Setting Up Network Printing
in the User's Guide.

faqs.question: How do I install my photo cartridge?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Note:
When installing the photo cartridge, make sure both sides of the cartridge are even with the back of the case. If one side sticks out slightly, as shown below, the printer may have printing problems, or the cartridge may leak or may not be recognized by the printer.
Shake the cartridge four or five times while it is still wrapped in its packaging.
Unwrap the cartridge.
Caution:
Don't touch the circuit board or remove the label. Install the photo cartridge immediately after you remove it from its package. If you leave a cartridge unpacked for a long time before using it, normal printing may not be possible.
Make sure the lever is in the release position as shown below. Then push in the cartridge, label side up. Push the center of the cartridge (shown below) until it latches. You may hear two clicks as each side of the cartridge latches into place.
Lever in the release position.
Area to push when installing ink cartridge.
(Click image to enlarge)
This photo shows the cartridge installed incorrectly. The cartridge is at a slight angle.
(Click image to enlarge)
Move the lever to the
Lock
position by sliding it in the direction shown. If you are having trouble getting the cartridge to lock in, hold the cartridge in place while you set the lever.
